items.title: Fourth pumping station to better protect Mississauga community from floods
items.summary: Plans to build a fourth automated pumping station in a northwest Mississauga community that’s experienced severe flooding for years are expected to take a big step forward later this month, the city says. With the third pumping station up and running in the Lisgar area of west Meadowvale since August, City of Mississauga staff “anticipate awarding the contract” for a long-awaited fourth facility in late November once the new term of city council convenes, Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden said in an update to constituents this week. The “critical” pieces of new infrastructure at Osprey Marsh will better protect people and their homes from major flooding in the city’s northwest corner, city officials have said. The third pumping station is located along Sixteen Mile Creek, immediately south of Doug Leavens Boulevard. McFadden noted in her latest community update that design of the fourth station, planned for the east edge of Osprey Marsh just south of Osprey Boulevard, is complete. ” In an update to constituents over the summer, McFadden said all four pumping stations, when operational, are designed to regulate the amount of stormwater within the Foundation Drain Collector system and automatically pump water out of the FDC sewers when it reaches a pre-determined level.

items.title: Road closures around Ridgeway Plaza in Mississauga
items.summary: A busy intersection in Mississauga’s west end is closed to traffic this week as crews continue to work on widening a main road. The City of Mississauga said it’s closing the Ninth Line/Platinum Drive intersection, to the immediate west of the large Ridgeway Plaza, between Nov. 2 and Nov. 7. The closure is necessary “to facilitate construction of the storm sewer system and oil-grit separator structure” and to allow workers “to safely complete the work while ensuring public safety and the safety of construction personnel,” the city said in its latest project update. Drivers can use Eglinton Avenue and Ridgeway Drive as alternate routes, project officials said, adding detour signs will be posted. The city noted it has coordinated with nearby businesses and schools to ensure the intersection closure isn’t disruptive. “In addition to the road closure requirements, additional flagmen will be placed at the entrance of the Autospa,” project officials said in their online update to the community. “Additionally, construction notices were hand delivered to the impacted businesses, including Autospa, the school, gas station and Tim Hortons. 7-kilometre stretch of Ninth Line between Derry Road and Eglinton Avenue to four lanes from its current two-lane configuration. When completed in late 2027, the new-look north-south road will feature more than the two extra lanes — it’ll also include new sidewalks, cycle tracks for bike riders, better bus stops and a host of additional attributes expected to “promote growth and allow more housing in the area,” the City of Mississauga said earlier.

items.title: Mississauga Bylaw Officials Remind Residents of New Fireworks Restrictions Ahead of Diwali
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is reminding residents to follow its fireworks bylaw as Diwali celebrations approach this week. According to the city, residents may only set off consumer fireworks on specific permitted holidays each year, and only on their own private property with the owner's permission. City officials said fireworks remain banned on all public property, including parks, streets, sidewalks and boulevards. This year, the city added Roman candles to its list of prohibited fireworks. Only adults 18 and older can buy fireworks, and only during the ten days leading up to an approved holiday, not on the holiday itself, the city said. The city is encouraging residents to consider quieter alternatives such as glow sticks and LED lights, which officials said are gentler on pets, wildlife and neighbours. Anyone who does set off permitted fireworks is asked to keep water on hand, supervise children closely and clean up thoroughly once the celebration ends. The reminder comes as part of the city's annual push to balance Diwali festivities with noise and fire safety concerns.

items.title: City of Mississauga Closes Ninth Line Intersection Near Ridgeway Plaza for Storm Sewer Work
items.summary: The City of Mississauga closed the intersection of Ninth Line and Platinum Drive, next to Ridgeway Plaza, from Nov. 2 to Nov. 7 to allow construction crews to keep working on the road's widening project. According to the city, the closure is needed to safely build a storm sewer system and an oil-grit separator structure at the intersection. City officials said drivers can detour via Eglinton Avenue and Ridgeway Drive while signs direct traffic around the closure. The city added that extra flaggers are posted at the entrance to the nearby Autospa, and that construction notices were hand-delivered to affected businesses, including Autospa, a nearby school, a gas station and a Tim Hortons. The broader project will widen a 7-kilometre stretch of Ninth Line between Derry Road and Eglinton Avenue from two lanes to four. Once finished in late 2027, the city said the rebuilt road will also include new sidewalks, cycle tracks and improved bus stops. Officials have said the upgrades are meant to support more housing and growth in the surrounding area.

items.title: Ontario Provincial Police Are Investigating a Fatal Early-Morning Crash in Puslinch That Killed Four Teenagers From the Mississauga Area
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say four teenagers are dead after a single-vehicle crash early Saturday morning on Watson Road South in Puslinch, near Guelph. According to OPP, the vehicle struck a guardrail before plunging into a ravine, killing a 19-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 19-year-old man from Brampton, and a 15-year-old girl from Milton. Two other teenage girls, aged 15 and 16, survived the crash but were taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries, police said. Investigators have not released a cause for the crash and have not said whether charges are expected. OPP confirmed the stretch of Watson Road South remained closed for several hours while officers investigated the scene. The force said updates would be provided as the investigation continues. The crash drew attention across the Peel and Halton regions given how many of the victims and survivors were local teenagers. Mississauga Insider will update this story if OPP releases further details.

items.title: Record-Early Stratospheric Warming Could Bring a Cold Snap to Ontario Despite Mild-Winter Forecasts
items.summary: According to Environment and Climate Change Canada research scientist Bill Merryfield, a disruption in the stratospheric polar vortex could send a cold blast into Ontario as early as mid to late November, cutting through what had been expected to be a milder winter. Merryfield told Metroland Media that the sudden stratospheric warming event stands out because of its timing, saying it has never occurred this early before. The disruption comes even as a strong El Nino pattern had led forecasters to predict a milder than usual winter for the province. Climate scientists say a sudden stratospheric warming event, which weakens the polar vortex high above the Arctic, can allow colder air to spill southward into Canada and the northern United States. According to the report, the exact timing and severity of the resulting cold snap remain uncertain, though models point to a possible arrival by late November or early December. Environment and Climate Change Canada says it will keep monitoring the disruption as the pattern develops over the coming weeks.

items.title: Danish Gift Retailer Flying Tiger Copenhagen Adds Fourth and Fifth Ontario Locations at Square One and CF Markville
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Danish gift retailer Flying Tiger Copenhagen is preparing to open a new store at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga sometime in November, though an exact opening date has not been announced. The outlet reports a fifth Ontario location is also under construction at CF Markville Mall in Markham, with that store expected to open around the same time. According to the report, the Mississauga and Markham locations add to three existing Ontario stores at Vaughan Mills, CF Toronto Eaton Centre and Scarborough Town Centre. Flying Tiger Copenhagen is known for compact, design-forward gift and novelty items, and the brand's expansion follows the arrival of similar retailers such as Miniso in the region. Mississauga.com says further details on both store openings, including exact dates, are expected closer to launch.
